text:
maya: Heads up — around 08:12 UTC we saw a staircase degradation in the SFO GPU pool: progressive node drops, not a single outage. Latency spiked for a subset of realtime slices and some requests were faned out to other regions. Investigating.

sanjay: seeing the same. metrics: GPU utilization jumped then P95 latency climbed. nodes started entering NotReady slowly. kube events show CNI flaps at approx 08:09.

leah: Ops-bot alerted at 08:13 with multiple pod restarts. Seems correlated with a noisy housekeeping job hitting network at the same time. @ops-bot can you paste the event summary?

ops-bot: incident: sfo-gpu-staircase-degradation detected. affected_slices: [realtime, batch-low-priority]. start_ts: 2331005400. automations triggered: weighted-shift -> partial-fanout to AMS, ORD.

tom: quick note — can we avoid broad fanout next time? fanout amplified tail latencies in AMS. We should prefer gradual shepherding with backpressure checks.

zara: agreed. Suggest adding a short cooldown + backpressure probe before shifting >10% traffic. Also add a cost guard to avoid unnecessary egress spikes.

dmitri: noted on cost. AMS egress increased 3x during the fanout window, cost bump ~estimated $420 for the hour. Also observed KV cache misses when requests moved regions.

maya: action items proposal: 1) update failover play to do stepwise shifts (5% -> 20% -> 50%) with 3-min probes, 2) require CNI health check pass before shifting, 3) add egress cost cap + alert, 4) run a dry-run on staging. Who owns?

leah: I can own the playbook edits (PR). I'll encode the stepwise percentages and probe queries.

sanjay: I'll add the CNI preflight check and the probe Grafana queries. Probe example:
```
# probe: ensure 95th latency < 250ms and packet-loss < 0.5% for 3m
promql: max_over_time(latency_p95[3m]) < 0.25 and (sum(packet_loss) by (region) / sum(tx_packets) by (region)) < 0.005
```

zara: I'll implement an egress-cost threshold in the routing controller: if estimated_hourly_egress > $200 then pause auto-shift and notify. Also adding a dry-run toggle for cost-heavy routes.

dmitri: for KV cache, add a warm-up window where we replicate small fraction of requests to new region 1m before shifting main traffic. That should reduce cold-cache miss spikes.

maya: good. leah, can you open the PR today? label it incident/2331005432 and link to this thread. Include rollback criteria and metric gates.

leah: will do. PR will include: changed shift percentages, probe promql, preflight CNI check, warm-up replicate step, and egress cap config snippet. ETA 18:00 UTC today.

tom: also recommend an item in runbook to coordinate with capacity team: edge warm pools should have a minimum reserve for cross-region acceptance to avoid cascading shortages.

maya: agree — add a reserve target (5% of pool) and a monitoring alert if reserve < 2%. sanjay, take point with infra capacity team?

sanjay: on it. I'll schedule a short sync and add the reserve config to the capacity playbook.

ops-bot: reminder: post-incident checklist created: update-runbook, cost-estimate, dry-run schedule, capacity-reserve config, telemetry queries.

maya: last: let's schedule a dry-run this week during low-traffic window. propose Fri 02:00 UTC. If no objections I'll book it.

zara: Friday fine for me. I'll prepare validation script for egress and cost simulation.

dmitri: I'll prep a KV warm-up harness for the dry-run.

leah: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/runbooks/pulls/482 — description and gates included. Please review.

maya: thanks everyone. I'll own the incident write-up and add the final action items to the incidents board. Closing thread for now — followups in PR and dry-run ticket. :white_check_mark:
